title: Add region-affinity claims transform and KMS consent cache for low-latency residency checks
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a tenant-region claims transformer and a KMS consent result cache to reduce residency verification latency and KMS call volume. No behavioural changes to existing RBAC rules; enable behind 'consent-cache' feature flag.
description: Motivation: Per-request residency checks and KMS provenance calls were a significant source of tail latency for tenant-scoped operations in high-throughput paths. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: (1) a deterministic claims transformer that normalizes and canonicalizes tenant region assertions (region-affinity claims) early in the request pipeline so RBAC v2 policy matching operates on a stable key, and (2) a short-lived KMS consent cache that memoizes the result of the residency/KMS consent verification (per-tenant+region+service tuple) to avoid repeated KMS calls for bursty workloads. Design: The claims transformer lives in pkg/rbac/claims_transform.go and implements a small policy-backed mapping that converts incoming adjacency claims (X-Claim-Region, geo-headers, and tenant metadata) into a canonical 'region_affinity' attribute used by policy rules. The KMS consent cache is implemented in pkg/kms/consent_cache.go and is bounded by entries per-tenant with TTL of 60s and a write-through refresh mechanism for cache misses. Both features are gated behind the 'consent-cache' runtime feature flag and a conservative default cache TTL. Migration & rollout: Feature is disabled by default. Steps: enable feature on staging for 48h, verify audit logs and policy matches, enable on canary hosts, then roll to prod with 10% steps. There is also a compatibility shim for legacy tenants that do not send region claims: transformer will synthesize from tenant profile lookup but the lookup is slow and still falls back to existing path. Testing: Unit tests cover claim normalization, cache eviction, and KMS error backoff. Integration test added to e2e/auth that asserts no extra KMS calls on repeated requests. Perf: microbench + canary A/B show 11-18% improvement in p50 and 20% reduction in KMS call rate for high-throughput tenants. Security: Cache keys are keyed by tenant ID and region and the cache is stored in memory per-process to avoid cross-tenant leakage; entries include opaque provenance tokens and are encrypted at rest when persisted by the host (no persistent writes by default). Audit: Every cache miss triggers an audit record identical to the legacy KMS flow; caches hits log a condensed audit pointer to the original verification event. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Perf numbers - [x] Docs updated - [x] Feature flag added Related: Linear ENG-1256, Security review SEC-342.
